contexts.text: That the diversions of charity are dinners, suppers, and social intercourse. General article.
That there are diversions of charity, which are various delights and pleasantnesses of the senses of the body, useful for the recreation of the mind. General article.

These are the diversions of everyone who is in an office or employment; and hence they may be called the diversions of offices or employments; but actually they are diversions of the affections from which each person works in his employment.
The diversions vary from the interior affection that is in them...
With those who do their work merely for the sake of their reputation... these diversions are similar in externals...
In those with whom there is an affection solely of gain, these diversions are also diversions, but fleshly...
From which it is evident what is the quality of their love in the above-mentioned diversions...
They do the works of their employment for the sake of diversions... When they are not in the diversions just enumerated, they are idlenesses...
